judged_text: The spread ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) merges the injected sentinel refresh_token:"refresh_token" over the credential's real refresh_token and the merged object is persisted via prisma.credential.update. In sharing mode every office365 refresh destroys the real refresh token in the DB; disabling sharing later (or a team credential with null userId falling back to direct refresh) leaves the integration permanently broken until re-authentication.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/office365calendar/lib/CalendarService.ts`, the refresh flow now uses `parseRefreshTokenResponse(responseJson, refreshTokenResponseSchema)`. In sharing mode (`APP_CREDENTIAL_SHARING_ENABLED && CALCOM_CREDENTIAL_SYNC_ENDPOINT`), `parseRefreshTokenResponse` validates against `minimumTokenResponseSchema` and then explicitly injects `refresh_token = "refresh_token"` when it is missing. Immediately after, the code does `o365AuthCredentials = { ...o365AuthCredentials, ...(tokenResponse.success && tokenResponse.data) };` and persists `o365AuthCredentials` via `prisma.credential.update(...)`. This will overwrite the real stored `refresh_token` with the injected sentinel value whenever the sync endpoint returns no refresh_token (as the comments indicate it should), permanently breaking later non-sharing refresh paths until re-auth.
